title: USB Drives Can Hold Up to 2 Terabytes
fact: USB flash drives can now hold up to 2 TB of data, though 64-256 GB are most common. They can store thousands of photos, videos, and documents.

title: Forests Create Their Own Weather
fact: Large forests create weather systems through transpiration, releasing huge amounts of water vapor that can form clouds and generate rainfall.

title: The Renaissance Produced Many Masterpieces
fact: The Renaissance produced masterpieces like the Mona Lisa, The Last Supper, and Michelangelo's David through 14th-17th century Europe.

title: A Group of Rams Is Called a Herd
fact: A group of rams is called a herd. Bighorn sheep rams charge at each other at speeds up to 40 mph during contests.

title: The Universe Is 93 Billion Light-Years Across
fact: The observable universe has a diameter of about 93 billion light-years. We can only see objects whose light has had time to reach us.

title: Your Bones Are Stronger Than Steel
fact: Bone is stronger than steel gram for gram. A matchbox-sized block of bone could support 10 tons of weight.

title: The Volga River Is Europe's Longest at 3,530 km
fact: The Volga River in Russia is Europe's longest river at 3,530 km. It flows into the Caspian Sea.

title: A Group of Stingrays Is Called a Fever
fact: A group of stingrays is called a fever. These graceful swimmers use their disc-shaped bodies to glide through the water.

title: The First Website Went Live in 1991
fact: Tim Berners-Lee's first website went live on August 6, 1991, at CERN. The URL was info.cern.ch and explained the World Wide Web project.

title: Trees Can Reduce Noise Pollution
fact: A 100-foot-wide forest belt can reduce noise by 50%, absorbing and blocking sound waves. This is why forests feel peaceful.

title: The Roman Colosseum Held 50,000 Spectators
fact: The Colosseum in Rome could hold between 50,000-80,000 spectators. It was built between 70-80 CE and used for gladiatorial contests.

title: A Group of Toads Is Called a Knot
fact: A group of toads is called a knot. Unlike frogs, toads have dry, warty skin and spend more time on land.

title: The Earth's Core Is as Hot as the Sun's Surface
fact: The inner core reaches temperatures of about 9,000°F (5,000°C), similar to the Sun's surface temperature of 9,900°F (5,500°C).

title: Your Nose Can Remember 50,000 Scents
fact: Humans can distinguish about 1 trillion different odors, though we only have about 400 types of smell receptors.

title: The Driest Place Is in Antarctica
fact: The McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica are the driest places on Earth, with virtually no ice or snow and extremely low humidity.

title: A Group of Badgers Is Called a Cete
fact: A group of badgers is called a cete. Honey badgers are considered the most fearless animals in the world.

title: The First Computer Virus Was Created in 1971
fact: The Creeper virus, created by Bob Thomas in 1971, was the first computer virus. It displayed 'I'm the Creeper: Catch me if you can!'

title: Forests Store Carbon for Thousands of Years
fact: Forests store carbon in their biomass and soil for hundreds to thousands of years. Old-growth forests store more carbon than younger ones.

title: The Library of Alexandria Burned in 48 BCE
fact: The Library of Alexandria, the ancient world's greatest repository of knowledge, was partially destroyed by fire during Julius Caesar's siege.

title: A Group of Pelicans Is Called a Squadron
fact: A group of pelicans is called a squadron. Brown pelicans can plunge dive from 60 feet to catch fish.

title: The Moon Orbits Earth Every 27.3 Days
fact: The Moon takes 27.3 days to orbit Earth, but the full lunar cycle (new moon to new moon) is 29.5 days due to Earth's orbital movement.

title: Your Bladder Can Hold 400-600ml of Fluid
fact: The average adult bladder can hold about 400-600ml of urine, about 2 cups. Signals to the brain about fullness occur around 200-300ml.

title: The Amazon River Has No Bridges
fact: The Amazon River, despite being over 4,000 miles long, has no permanent bridges. The river's width makes bridging impractical.

title: A Group of Quail Is Called a Covey
fact: A group of quail is called a covey. Quail are known for their distinctive head plumes and are popular game birds.

title: WiFi Signals Travel at the Speed of Light
fact: WiFi signals travel at the speed of light (about 300,000 km/s), but interference and obstacles can slow them down.

title: Trees Absorb 48 Pounds of CO2 Per Year
fact: A single tree can absorb about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year and release enough oxygen for two people to breathe.

title: The Treaty of Versailles Was Signed in 1919
fact: The Treaty of Versailles officially ended World War I in 1919. It imposed heavy penalties on Germany.

title: A Group of Rooks Is Called a Parliament
fact: A group of rooks is called a parliament. Rooks are intelligent birds known for their ability to solve complex problems.

title: There Are More Stars Than Grains of Sand
fact: Scientists estimate there are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.

title: Your Brain Uses Electricity
fact: The human brain generates about 20 watts of electrical power, enough to power a small light bulb. Neurons fire at speeds up to 268 mph.

title: Lake Baikal Contains 20% of Unfrozen Freshwater
fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia contains about 20% of Earth's unfrozen fresh surface water. It's also the world's deepest and oldest lake.

title: A Group of Storks Is Called a Muster
fact: A group of storks is called a muster. Storks are known for their long-distance migrations.

title: The First Computer Mouse Was Invented in 1964
fact: Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in 1964 at Stanford Research Institute. It was made of wood with two perpendicular wheels.

title: Forests Help Prevent Floods
fact: Forests absorb rainfall and slow runoff, reducing flood risks. Tree roots absorb water and release it slowly, maintaining stream flows.

title: The First Olympics Were Held in 776 BCE
fact: The ancient Olympic Games began in 776 BCE at Olympia, Greece. They were held every four years and honored Zeus.

title: A Group of Vultures Is Called a Wake
fact: A group of vultures is called a wake. These birds play an important ecological role as nature's cleanup crew.

title: The Sun Takes 225 Million Years to Orbit Milky Way
fact: The Sun takes about 225 million Earth years to complete one orbit around the Milky Way's center. This is called a galactic year.

title: Your Blood Contains 0.8 Ounces of Iron
fact: Your body contains about 3-4 grams of iron, mostly in hemoglobin. That's enough to make a small nail about 2 inches long.

title: The Grand Canyon Took 3-6 Million Years to Form
fact: The Grand Canyon formed over 3-6 million years through the combined action of the Colorado River and erosion.

title: A Group of Lemurs Is Called a Conspiracy
fact: A group of lemurs is called a conspiracy. Ring-tailed lemurs spend more time on the ground than other lemur species.

title: Java Was Originally Called Oak
fact: Java was originally named Oak by James Gosling in 1991, after a tree outside his office. It was renamed Java because Oak was already trademarked.

title: Forests Are Home to 1.6 Billion People
fact: About 1.6 billion people globally depend on forests for their livelihoods, including food, medicine, fuel, and income.

title: The Crusade to Capture Jerusalem Occurred 1099
fact: The First Crusade culminated in 1099 with the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of Crusader states in the Holy Land.

title: A Group of Baboons Is Called a Troop
fact: A group of baboons is called a troop. Baboons live in complex social hierarchies with clear dominance structures.

title: The Moon Is Moving Away From Earth
fact: The Moon recedes from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year. In 600 million years, total solar eclipses will no longer occur.

title: Your Brain Has a Storage Capacity of 2.5 Petabytes
fact: Your brain's memory storage capacity is estimated at about 2.5 petabytes (2.5 million gigabytes), equivalent to 3 million hours of TV shows.

title: The Dead Sea Is 430 Meters Below Sea Level
fact: The Dead Sea's shoreline is the lowest exposed point on Earth's surface at 430.5 meters below sea level. It's one of the saltiest bodies of water.

title: A Group of Peacocks Is Called a Party
fact: A group of peacocks is called a party or ostentation. Only males have the colorful tail feathers used for courtship displays.

title: The First Operating System Was Created in 1964
fact: The first operating system, CTSS (Compatible Time-Sharing System), was developed at MIT in 1964, allowing multiple users to access a computer.

title: Trees Can Reduce Air Pollution
fact: Trees absorb pollutants like ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and sulfur dioxide through their leaves. A single tree can remove 0.4-1.5 pounds of pollutants annually.

title: The Great Wall of China Was Built Over 2,000 Years
fact: Construction on the Great Wall began in the 7th century BCE and continued until the Ming Dynasty in the 17th century.

title: A Group of Woodpeckers Is Called a Descent
fact: A group of woodpeckers is called a descent. These birds can peck up to 20 times per second to find insects and create nest cavities.

title: Jupiter Has 95 Known Moons
fact: Jupiter has 95 known moons as of 2023, the most of any planet. The four largest are the Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

title: Your Body Has 37.2 Trillion Cells
fact: The human body contains approximately 37.2 trillion cells, with 200 different types. Most are red blood cells, which live for about 120 days.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro Has Three Volcanic Cones
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro has three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira. Kibo is the highest and could erupt again despite being dormant.

title: A Group of Newts Is Called a Benison
fact: A group of newts is called a benison. Newts are salamanders that spend part of their lives in water and part on land.

title: The First Smartphone Was IBM Simon in 1994
fact: The IBM Simon Personal Communicator, released in 1994, is considered the first smartphone. It had a touchscreen, email, and could send faxes.

title: Forests Provide 75% of Urban Freshwater
fact: About 75% of accessible freshwater for urban areas comes from forested watersheds. Forests filter and regulate water flow.

title: The World Wide Web Was Invented in 1989
fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN, combining hypertext with the internet to create a global information space.

title: A Group of Kangaroos Is Called a Mob
fact: A group of kangaroos is called a mob. They use their strong tails for balance when hopping and as a fifth leg when standing.

title: Saturn Would Float in Water
fact: Saturn is the least dense planet; if you could find a bathtub big enough, it would float. Its density is less than that of water.

title: Your Brain Is More Active at Night
fact: Your brain is actually more active during sleep than during the day. This is when the brain processes memories and repairs itself.

title: The Largest Salt Flat Is in Bolivia
fact: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the world's largest salt flat at 4,086 square miles. During wet season, it becomes the world's largest mirror.

title: A Group of Moles Is Called a Labor
fact: A group of moles is called a labor. Moles can dig up to 18 feet per hour through soil searching for insects.

title: The First WiFi Network Operated in 1997
fact: The first WiFi standard (802.11) was released in 1997, enabling wireless data transfer at 2 Mbps. Modern WiFi can reach 10+ Gbps.

title: Trees Can Cool the Air Through Transpiration
fact: A single large tree can transpire 100 gallons of water daily, which cools the surrounding air by up to 10 degrees Fahrenheit.

title: The Suez Canal Took 10 Years to Build
fact: The Suez Canal took 10 years to build (1859-1869) and is 120 miles long. It connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

title: A Group of Turtles Is Called a Bale
fact: A group of sea turtles is called a bale. Some sea turtle species can hold their breath for up to 7 hours while sleeping underwater.

title: The Sun Contains 99.86% of Solar System Mass
fact: The Sun contains 99.86% of all mass in the solar system. Jupiter accounts for most of the remaining 0.14%.

title: Your Heart Beats 100,000 Times Per Day
fact: Your heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood. This adds up to about 3 billion beats in a lifetime.

title: The Amazon River Is Wider Than the Next 10 Rivers Combined
fact: The Amazon River's width varies from 1 to 30 miles, making it wider than the next 10 largest rivers combined at their mouths.

title: A Group of Lizards Is Called a Lounge
fact: A group of lizards is called a lounge. Some lizards can detach their tails to escape predators and then regrow them.

title: The First Digital Camera Had 0.1 Megapixels
fact: The first commercial digital camera in 1990 had only 0.14 megapixels and cost $10,000. Modern smartphones have 100+ megapixel cameras.

title: Forests Can Filter 85% of Particulate Matter
fact: Trees and forests can filter up to 85% of particulate matter from the air, significantly improving air quality in urban areas.

title: The Napoleonic Wars Lasted 12 Years
fact: The Napoleonic Wars (1803-1815) lasted about 12 years and involved most of Europe. Napoleon commanded forces across multiple continents.

title: A Group of Eagles Is Called a Convocation
fact: A group of eagles is called a convocation. Bald eagles mate for life and return to the same nest year after year.

title: The Milky Way Will Collide with Andromeda
fact: The Milky Way and Andromeda are approaching each other at 250,000 mph and will merge in about 4.5 billion years.

title: Your Brain Weighs About 3 Pounds
fact: An adult brain weighs about 3 pounds (1.4 kg). It contains 86 billion neurons, each connected to thousands of others.

title: The Amazon Rainforest Gets 9 Feet of Rain Annually
fact: The Amazon rainforest receives about 9 feet (2.7 meters) of rainfall per year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

title: A Group of Wolves Is Called a Pack
fact: Wolves live in family groups called packs, typically with 6-10 members. The pack is led by an alpha pair, usually the parents.

title: The First Bitcoin Transaction Was in 2009
fact: The first Bitcoin transaction occurred on January 12, 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto sent 10 BTC to Hal Finney.

title: Trees Produce Clouds Through Transpiration
fact: Large forests release so much water vapor through transpiration that they create their own cloud cover and influence regional weather patterns.

title: The Panama Canal Opened in 1914
fact: The Panama Canal opened on August 15, 1914, after a decade of construction. It handles over 12,000 ships annually.

title: A Group of Rhinoceros Is Called a Crash
fact: A group of rhinoceros is called a crash. These endangered animals are threatened by poaching for their horns.

title: Black Holes Can Sing in B-Flat
fact: In 2003, astronomers detected sound waves from a black hole in the Perseus cluster. The note is B-flat, 57 octaves below middle C.

title: Your Brain Is 60% Fat
fact: Your brain is about 60% fat, making it one of the fattiest organs in the body. This fat is essential for brain cell structure and function.

title: The Atacama Desert Has the Clearest Skies
fact: The Atacama Desert in Chile has the clearest skies on Earth, making it ideal for astronomical observatories.

title: A Group of Pigeons Is Called a Kit
fact: A group of pigeons is called a kit. Pigeons have excellent navigational abilities and were used as messenger birds.

title: The First Computer Program Was Written in 1843
fact: Ada Lovelace wrote the first computer program in 1843 for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine. It calculated Bernoulli numbers.

title: Forests Reduce Urban Noise by 50%
fact: Trees and vegetation can reduce urban noise pollution by up to 50% by absorbing and scattering sound waves.

title: The First Moon Landing Cost $25.4 Billion
fact: The Apollo program cost about $25.4 billion (about $180 billion today), representing about 4% of US GDP at its peak.

title: A Group of Porcupines Is Called a Prickle
fact: A group of porcupines is called a prickle. Despite their dangerous quills, porcupines are generally docile and try to avoid confrontation.

title: The Sun's Light Takes 8 Minutes to Reach Earth
fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, traveling at 186,000 miles per second.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Calories
fact: Despite being only 2% of body weight, your brain uses about 20% of your caloric intake, making it extremely energy-intensive.

title: Lake Superior Has 78.6 Trillion Gallons of Water
fact: Lake Superior contains about 78.6 trillion gallons of water, enough to cover North and South America in 1 foot of water.

title: A Group of Cheetahs Is Called a Coalition
fact: A group of cheetahs is called a coalition. Male cheetahs often form coalitions to protect their territory and hunting grounds.

title: WiFi Passwords Originated from Banking
fact: The concept of passwords originated from ancient Roman military watchwords. Modern digital passwords evolved from computer time-sharing systems in the 1960s.

title: Forests Produce 50% of Earth's Oxygen
fact: Forests and phytoplankton together produce about 50% of Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis.

title: The Suez Canal Was Built by 1.5 Million Workers
fact: The construction of the Suez Canal involved approximately 1.5 million workers from various countries, including Egypt, France, and Britain.

title: A Group of Barracudas Is Called a Battery
fact: A group of barracudas is called a battery. These fearsome predators can accelerate up to 36 mph in short bursts.
